effects: The signer sends `assets` ftUSD (0xD6DD…0285, the vault's ASSET) to the vault, using an earlier approval.
`receiver` gets `assets` sftUSD vault shares (1:1). These shares are the staking position that earns FT rewards.
The vault deposits the ftUSD into the external yieldWrapper. This uses the vault's own funds and takes nothing more from the signer.
The receiver's reward checkpoint is settled. No asset moves.
formats.shown: "Stake 9.020293 ftUSD", with the amount in ftUSD and the receiver address as fields.

findings.title: deposit: the sentence leaves out the receiver who gets the sftUSD staking position.
findings.evidence: EpochRewardsVault.sol deposit → _deposit: `_mint(to, shares)`. Descriptor interpolatedIntent "Stake {assets}". The Receiver field is shown separately (case 0: Receiver 0xd8dA…6045).
findings.fix: Use interpolatedIntent "Stake {assets} for {receiver}" and mention sftUSD, e.g. intent "Stake ftUSD for sftUSD".

findings.title: deposit: the receiver address types are only wallet/eoa, but any non-zero address, including a contract, is accepted.
findings.evidence: deposit only checks `if (receiver == address(0)) revert ZeroAddress();`. Descriptor receiver params types ["wallet","eoa"].
findings.fix: Widen `types` to include "contract", or remove the restriction.

formats.key: withdraw(uint256 assets, address receiver, address owner)
effects: `assets` sftUSD shares are burned from `owner` (1:1). If owner is not the signer, the signer's share allowance from owner is spent.
The vault calls yieldWrapper.withdraw(assets, receiver), which sends `assets` ftUSD to `receiver` now or puts the withdrawal in a queue (a queueId is returned).
The owner's FT reward checkpoint is settled. Accrued rewards stay claimable.
formats.shown: "Unstake 9.020293 ftUSD", with the amount in ftUSD and the receiver and owner addresses as fields.

findings.title: withdraw: the payout may be queued in the external yieldWrapper, so ftUSD may not arrive in this transaction.
findings.evidence: EpochRewardsVault.sol _withdrawWithQueueIds: `queueIdTo = yieldWrapper.withdraw(assets, receiver);` and withdrawWithQueueId's comment says "queue ID (0 when immediate)". The devdoc says "exits still rely on the external `yieldWrapper` behavior". The yieldWrapper 0xA974…8f71 source is not in the directory.
findings.fix: If withdrawals are often queued, say "Request unstake" or add a notice that ftUSD may arrive after a queue.

findings.title: withdraw: the sentence leaves out the receiver and the sftUSD burned from the owner.
findings.evidence: _withdrawWithQueueIds: `_burn(owner, shares)` and `yieldWrapper.withdraw(assets, receiver)`. Descriptor interpolatedIntent "Unstake {assets}". Receiver and Owner are separate fields.

findings.title: withdraw: the receiver and owner address types are only wallet/eoa, but the code accepts contracts.
findings.evidence: withdraw only rejects address(0). Descriptor types ["wallet","eoa"] on both receiver and owner.

effects: All of the signer's settled FT rewards are paid to `to`. The payout is capped at the vault's FT balance, and any unpaid rest stays accrued to the signer.
The signer's reward checkpoint is settled. The fee is zero on this path.
formats.shown: "Claim FT to 0xd8dA…6045", with the recipient address as a field.

findings.title: claim: the FT amount comes from on-chain accrual and cannot be shown from the calldata.
findings.evidence: EpochRewardsVault.sol _claim: `uint256 claimable = user.ftAccrued; ... paidGross = claimable <= bal ? claimable : bal; FT.safeTransfer(to, paidToUser);`
findings.fix: None in the descriptor. The wallet could show previewClaimable(signer).

findings.title: claim: the recipient address types are only wallet/eoa, but `to` can be any non-zero address.
findings.evidence: _claim: `if (to == address(0)) revert ZeroAddress();`. Descriptor to params types ["wallet","eoa"].

couldNotCheck: withdraw(uint256,address,address) calls yieldWrapper 0xA974A72F3f2Cb18A343FE676e4feDEE8e0248f71 `withdraw(assets, receiver)`. Its source is not in the directory, so I could not check whether the receiver gets ftUSD at once, gets it in full, or only gets a queue entry.

deposit(uint256 assets, address receiver.worst: deposit: the sentence leaves out the receiver who gets the sftUSD staking position.

withdraw(uint256 assets, address receive.worst: withdraw: the sentence leaves out the receiver and the sftUSD burned from the owner.

claim(address to).worst: claim: the recipient address types are only wallet/eoa, but `to` can be any non-zero address.

summary.worst: deposit: the sentence leaves out the receiver who gets the sftUSD staking position.
